key_insight: Large language models can use self‑generated samples as replay data during continued training to almost eliminate catastrophic forgetting; however, forgetting reappears when the model lacks sufficient capacity or when optimization dynamics are unfavorable.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on storing real exemplars to prevent forgetting in continual learning by showing self‑generated replay is an effective alternative, while characterizing when it fails (capacity and optimization limits).
method: Generate synthetic replay examples from the model's own distribution and interleave them with new‑task training.
Compare forgetting outcomes against baselines (no replay, stored exemplar replay) across model sizes and optimization settings.
Analyze the role of model capacity and optimization dynamics in enabling or limiting the effectiveness of self‑generated replay.
impact: Enables practical, privacy‑friendly continual learning for language models without large exemplar stores, but signals practitioners to ensure adequate model capacity and appropriate optimization to realize these gains.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the self‑generated replay loop: model → sample generation → mix with new data → continued training
Bar chart comparing task performance retention: no replay vs stored exemplar replay vs self‑generated replay
Heatmap or line plot showing forgetting vs model capacity (size) and vs optimization hyperparameters
Schematic illustrating failure modes: low capacity/poor optimization → residual forgetting
paper_title: Forgetting in Language Models: Capacity, Optimization, and Self-Generated Replay
paper_authors: Martin Marek, Dongkyu Cho, Shikai Qiu, Rumi Chunara, Pavel Izmailov
